title: Inference engine survey (closed book)
description: Questions on the paper 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models: Perspectives on Optimization and Efficiency' (GLB_Gen_AI_Framework/RAG/sample2.pdf), with the ground truth from RAG_eval.xlsx. Asked without the paper, so it tests what the model knows about LLM serving, and whether it admits what it does not know.

questions.question: In the 2025 survey 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models', how many inference engines are evaluated, and how many are open-source versus commercial?
The survey 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models' compares engines on six evaluation dimensions. What are they?
questions.reference: General-purpose, ease of deployment, ease of use, latency-aware, throughput-aware, and scalability.

questions.question: In the survey 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models', which organization types maintain the 21 open-source engines, and how many engines does each type maintain?
questions.reference: Academic (6), startup (6), big tech (5) and community (4).

questions.question: What public GitHub repository do the authors of 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models' provide to track developments in LLM inference engines?
What are the two main phases of LLM inference, and which latency metric does each phase mainly affect?
questions.reference: Prefill mainly affects time to first token (TTFT); decode mainly affects the time between tokens (TBT / ITL).

questions.question: How is end-to-end latency of an LLM request expressed in terms of time to first token and time between tokens?
questions.reference: Latency = TTFT + (TBT x number of output tokens).

questions.question: How does Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) differ from Multi-Query Attention (MQA) in how the KV cache is shared?
questions.reference: MQA shares a single set of keys and values across all query heads; GQA shares keys and values within groups of heads, so the number of groups trades memory for quality.

questions.question: What attention mechanism did DeepSeek-V2 introduce, and what is its key advantage?
questions.reference: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), which compresses keys and values into a shared latent vector, shrinking the KV cache while keeping accuracy.

questions.question: What is the core backend of Ollama, and what are the two main components of its architecture?
questions.reference: llama.cpp; a client (command line) and a server (HTTP server with the llama.cpp backend).

questions.question: What is PagedAttention in vLLM, and what problem does it solve?
questions.reference: It stores the KV cache in non-contiguous blocks (pages), like OS virtual memory, which avoids memory fragmentation so more requests fit and throughput rises.

questions.question: What are the three kernel types offered by bitnet.cpp, and what hardware do they target?
questions.reference: I2_S, TL1 and TL2, optimised for x86 and ARM CPUs.

questions.question: What is RadixAttention in SGLang, and how does it differ from vLLM's PagedAttention?
questions.reference: RadixAttention keeps cached KV entries in a radix tree so shared prefixes are reused across requests; PagedAttention manages memory allocation in non-contiguous blocks.

questions.question: Name four batching strategies used by LLM inference engines that include nano-batching, and say which engine introduced nano-batching.
questions.reference: Dynamic batching, continuous batching, nano-batching and chunked prefill; nano-batching was introduced by NanoFlow.

questions.question: In 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models', which tool was used to benchmark inference performance, and why was an OpenAI API-compatible approach chosen?
questions.reference: GuideLLM; an OpenAI-compatible interface reduces implementation-dependent differences, so the comparison is fair, reproducible and reflects end-to-end serving as users see it.

questions.question: In the server-side full-precision evaluation of 'A Survey on Inference Engines for Large Language Models', which four engines consistently performed best on NVIDIA H100 GPUs?
